CAUSE: `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=...)` in `run_pytest` does not guarantee text output on timeout. `subprocess.TimeoutExpired.stdout` and `.stderr` can be bytes even with `text=True`; when one stream is empty, `(exc.stdout or "") + (exc.stderr or "")` mixes bytes and str and raises `TypeError` before the gate can return its timeout result.

Evidence: the timeout handler is in `app/merge_test_gate.py`, `run_pytest`. I reproduced both failure directions with timed-out Python subprocesses using the same `capture_output=True, text=True` settings: stdout-only produced `bytes + ""`; stderr-only produced `"" + bytes`, matching the reported error exactly. A direct `run_pytest` attempt timed out during pytest startup and returned normally, so I did not reproduce the crash through pytest itself.

Fix recommendation: normalize each captured stream independently before concatenating—for example, decode bytes with UTF-8 and `errors="replace"`, while leaving strings unchanged. This handles either stream being absent or bytes and preserves the intended inconclusive timeout result.
